ClickHouse 26.9.16.11 (official apt deb, arm64, installed on the VM; listens on 127.0.0.1:8123) and ClickHouse 26.3.48.2 (docker image clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.3, digest sha256:89556e4d21c2ab6a7ebdacfeeb0bbfc47addd912692149db8f184e19a8ba243a, docker.io 29.1.3 installed on the VM only, container listens on 172.18.0.2:8123); measured with strace 6.19 (-f -yy -xx -ttt, server and client side), curl 8.18.0, Python 3.14.4 http.client and raw sockets, clickhouse-compressor (LZ4 frame for rs_insert).

# T1 measurement: ClickHouse HTTP interface write/read boundaries
# Do not edit by hand. Re-run the procedure at the end of this file to regenerate. Companion fixtures: http/<scenario>.records.

== Environment
- Host: OrbStack Linux VM edc-ch, Ubuntu 26.04 arm64, kernel 7.0.14-orbstack, 15 CPUs. Linux only; the macOS host was not used.
- 26.9 server: deb install, started by hand in a private UTS namespace with hostname "fixture-host" (same as stage 1, see boundaries.txt). HTTP port 8123 on 127.0.0.1. The client (curl or python) ran on the VM host and connected to 127.0.0.1:8123.
- 26.3 server: docker container edc-ch263 (hostname fixture-host, docker network edc-net 172.18.0.0/16, container IP 172.18.0.2, published as 18123->8123 and 19000->9000 so the 26.9 server stayed on 8123/9000). The client ran in the network namespace of a second container edc-client (172.18.0.3, entrypoint "sleep infinity", same image) through "nsenter -t <pid of edc-client> -n strace ... curl http://172.18.0.2:8123/..." . This is the same path as production: app container to ClickHouse container, container IP, no docker-proxy.
- User edc / password edc-fixture (fake) on both servers. Table default.t (a UInt32, b String) ENGINE=MergeTree ORDER BY a.
- Server tracing: strace -f -p <server pid> -yy -xx -ttt -s 2097152 -e trace=read,recvfrom,recvmsg,readv,write,sendto,sendmsg,writev (26.3: inside the container network namespace so -yy resolves the sockets). Client tracing: strace -f -yy -xx -ttt -s 2097152 with the same -e list in front of the command. Only syscalls on the HTTP socket (server: local port 8123, client: peer port 8123) are kept.
- Syscalls seen: sendto and recvfrom only (curl, python http.client, ClickHouse). One syscall = one record, which is what the BPF hook sees as one tcp_sendmsg/tcp_recvmsg (stage 1 relied on the same equality). TCP segment boundaries were not measured.
- strace slows both sides. Timestamps order records and give rough latencies, they are not benchmarks. Client read boundaries depend on the client and on timing.
- Defaults seen on both servers (system.settings): enable_http_compression=1, http_response_buffer_size=0, async_insert=1, wait_for_async_insert=1, async_insert_use_adaptive_busy_timeout=1, async_insert_busy_timeout_min_ms=50, async_insert_busy_timeout_max_ms=200, http_max_uri_size=1048576, http_max_field_value_size=131072. network_compression_method: LZ4 on 26.3; the compression frames seen on the 26.9 server start with method byte 0x90 (ZSTD), on 26.3 with 0x82 (LZ4).
- Reader clients: curl reads with a 102400-byte buffer. Python http.client reads through a buffered reader (reads of 2 to 338832 bytes seen). The real production client (clickhouse-rs 0.15.1, Rust) was not run; its User-Agent and header set were copied into curl (rs_insert, rs_select, rs_select_midstream_error). Whether clickhouse-rs sends the same bytes is 추정.

== Fixture format
- One file per scenario: http/<scenario>.records. Sections start with a "# version: <version> deb|docker <digest>" line. Replay each section on its own. A section can hold several runs ("# run <n>: <label>", "# command: <command>"); each run is one or more connections in time order.
- Record line: "<server|client> <send|recv> <total bytes> <hex>". hex = first min(total,4096) bytes. Client and server lines are interleaved by syscall time: filter by side. A client send equals a server recv byte for byte (checked), a server send equals a client recv.
- Deviation from "first 4096 bytes": when total > 4096 and no framing element (status line, header line, chunk size line, chunk CRLF, terminal chunk) and no "__exception__" marker starts between byte 56 and byte 4096 of the record, the hex holds only the first 64 bytes. The omitted bytes are plain chunk data or request body. T3 pads the hex with 'x' up to min(total,4096) bytes. Such padding cannot create a fake CRLF. A loader must not assume len(hex)/2 == min(total,4096).
- Lines are not wrapped, a line can be 8 KB.
- 'DATA/' in a command line means /tmp/ch/data/ on the VM (files made by "m.py data").

== Table legend
element names in "pattern=[...]" (one token per record, "|" separates records, "xN" repeats the same record kind N times, "+" joins elements that start in the same record, "~" prefix = the record starts in the middle of an element):
  st = status line, h = one header line (hxN = N header lines), he = blank line that ends the headers, csz = chunk size line, data = chunk data, crlf = CRLF after chunk data, last = terminal chunk "0 CRLF CRLF" (5 bytes), rl = request line, body = Content-Length body.
"rec<i>@<o>/<n>" = record index i (0-based, in the connection and direction), offset o in the record, record size n. "in4096=True" = the element ends inside the first 4096 bytes of that record. "alone5=True" = the terminal chunk is a record of its own with exactly 5 bytes. "walk4096" = result of walking status line, headers, chunk sizes and the terminal chunk with only the first 4096 bytes of every record visible (OK, or LOST(reason)). "walk4096_ok" is the same for requests. Times are strace start-of-call stamps relative to the first client send.
A server connection is shown as "server send" (response) and "server recv" (request); the client side as "client recv" and "client send".

== Findings that differ from the plan or add to it (for T2/T3)
1. Header block is NOT one send. The server sends the status line (17 bytes for 200 OK, 24 for 404, 36 for 500; 25 bytes for "100 Continue"), then the 22 bytes "X-ClickHouse-Summary: ", then the JSON value (183-210 bytes), then CRLF (2 bytes), then all remaining headers in one send (537-688 bytes), and for a HEAD /ping the status line and the headers (211-234 bytes) are two sends. The header end is at most 688 bytes into its record (largest over all runs). The headers never span the 4096 limit.
2. Body framing on the server: chunk size line (3-8 bytes), chunk data, CRLF (2 bytes), each as its own send; the terminal chunk "0 CRLF CRLF" is its own 5-byte send in 31 of 31 chunked responses that complete, on both versions. Chunk data sends are up to 1048576 bytes (plain results and gzip/compress=1) or 130818 bytes (throwIf test).
3. Error before the first output byte (SELECT * FROM missing_table, 404; throwIf before the first flush, 500): normal chunked response with the error text as one chunk, X-ClickHouse-Exception-Code in the headers, terminal chunk present.
4. Error after output started (HTTP status stays 200): the exception block is one chunk of its own, 365-366 bytes, sent as one send after its 5-byte chunk size line, then a 2-byte CRLF send. Layout: "\r\n__exception__\r\n<tag 16 letters>\r\n<message>\n<message length> <tag>\r\n__exception__\r\n". The tag equals the X-ClickHouse-Exception-Tag header. The marker "__exception__" appears twice but only the first one is followed by the tag. NO terminal chunk follows: the server closes the connection (curl exit code 18, client recv returned 0).
5. The server closes the connection after a mid-stream error and after an HTTP/1.0 response; for HTTP/1.0 (curl --http1.0) the response is "HTTP/1.0 200 OK" with "Connection: Close" and no Content-Length and no chunking, so the body end is only the close.
6. "Expect: 100-continue" (curl, 2 MiB POST): the server sends "HTTP/1.1 100 Continue" as its own 25-byte send 2.4 ms (26.9) / 2.8 ms (26.3) after the request headers, then reads the body, then sends the final response. The upload took about 19 ms (26.9) / 29 ms (26.3) under strace. The server recv splits the body into 7 (26.9) or 9 (26.3) records.
7. Chunked request (python encode_chunked, and curl "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" in rs_insert): the client sends headers and chunks in separate sends or in one send, the server recv coalesces them (chunked_request: client 5 sends, server 1 recv of 269/270 bytes). In rs_insert (curl, 5166 byte LZ4 frame) the headers (233 bytes) and the whole chunked body are ONE send/recv of 5412 bytes; the chunk size line is at offset 233, the chunk data is 5166 bytes, and the chunk CRLF and the terminal chunk are the last 7 bytes of the same record, past byte 4096, so the request walk with 4096 bytes cannot reach the end of the request (walk4096_ok=False).
8. A request with a 5 KB URL (x_long_url) is one 5161-byte record; the header end is past byte 4096, the SQL is cut, the request walk is lost. The response side is unaffected.
9. Default query SQL rules verified through system.query_log on both versions (query_ids edc-t1-plus, edc-t1-body, edc-t1-post, edc-t1-dup): '+' in the URL query parameter becomes a space and %2B becomes '+' (SELECT 1 AS a, 'p+q' AS b, 'x y'); with a body the text is "<query parameter>\n<body>" (query=SELECT 42 and body " FORMAT JSONCompact" gave "SELECT 42\n FORMAT JSONCompact"); a query parameter with no body still gets a trailing "\n"; with a repeated query parameter only the first is used; without the parameter the body is the whole SQL.
10. The compression frames of "compress=1" answers: 26.3 uses LZ4 (method byte 0x82), 26.9 uses ZSTD (0x90). This matters for the mid-stream error (see "compress=1 verdict").
11. clickhouse-compressor --codec LZ4 output was accepted by "decompress=1" on both versions (1000 RowBinary rows inserted, count checked). Whether it matches clickhouse-rs bytes is 추정.
12. Records of the same response read by curl: for results up to a few KB the client reads mirror the server sends (some adjacent small sends are merged, for example "csz+data" as one 5-byte read). For results of 64 KB and more curl reads 56 to 102400 bytes and most reads start in the middle of chunk data (big: 778 reads on 26.9 for 465 server sends).

== A1..A9 verdicts
A1 (server send unit, terminal chunk separate): CONFIRMED on 26.9 and 26.3. Every one of the 31 completed chunked responses per version ends with a lone 5-byte record at offset 0; the sends are: status line, "X-ClickHouse-Summary: ", JSON, CRLF, other headers, size line, data, CRLF, ..., terminal chunk (finding 1 and 2). Sizes differ only by the version string and header count. TCP segmentation was not measured, so a BPF record = one send is the assumption stated in Environment.
A2 (client reads mix): CONFIRMED and client dependent. curl: small results mirror the server; big, wait_end, gzip and compress=1 results of 18 KB and more put the chunk size lines and the terminal chunk inside reads of 18-95 KB (see table, tail lines). Python http.client on big: 439 reads (26.9) / 414 (26.3), last read is the lone 5-byte terminal chunk but the chunk size lines in between are beyond 4096 of their records, so the walk is lost anyway.
A3 (container network): PARTLY CONFIRMED. Direct path from edc-client (172.18.0.3) to edc-ch263 (172.18.0.2:8123): the server socket is 172.18.0.2:8123 <-> 172.18.0.3:<port>, the client socket sits in the client container network namespace, and docker-proxy shows no socket activity at all during the request. Published path (host curl to 127.0.0.1:18123): TWO sockets: client <-> docker-proxy (127.0.0.1:18123) and docker-proxy <-> server (172.18.0.1:<port> -> 172.18.0.2:8123), so the server sees peer 172.18.0.1. docker-proxy moves the bytes with splice(2) (socket -> pipe -> socket), not with recv/send. NOT TESTED in T1: whether the kernel hooks of edc see the sockets in the container network namespaces (strace only); the splice path is relevant for T7.
A4 (pipelining): PARTLY REFUTED. Two requests in ONE send (one 354-byte recv on the server): only the first is answered; the second got no response within 4 s, on both versions (python pipe_one). Two requests in two sends before the first response (sleep(1) request, then SELECT 2 50 ms later): both answered in order, the second response starts about 7 ms after the first ends (pipe_two). So a FIFO in T3 gets a permanent unanswered entry in the first case. /ping and queries on one keep-alive connection work in order (keepalive_ping run 0).
A5 (compressed mid-stream error): PARTLY REFUTED, see the compress=1 verdict. gzip (Accept-Encoding + enable_http_compression): 0 of 2 versions show the marker.
A6 (async insert): CONFIRMED. Both servers have async_insert=1 and wait_for_async_insert=1 for user edc. async_wait1: first response record +77.1 ms (26.9) / +75.5 ms (26.3), the Summary elapsed_ns is 72.7 / 71.2 ms. async_wait0: +6.7 ms / +12.2 ms. The flush came at about 75 ms, not at the 200 ms busy timeout; async_insert_use_adaptive_busy_timeout=1 with min 50 ms and max 200 ms is the likely reason (추정). A plain insert without the async parameters (insert_format +81.6 ms, insert_values +84.1 ms to the first response record on 26.9) behaves like wait=1, as the defaults say.
A7 (docker): docker.io installed on the VM with user approval; the 26.3 image was used, no tgz fallback.
A8 (request line and headers within 4096): CONFIRMED for normal requests (the largest request header block measured: 289 bytes, curl/python/clickhouse-rs shapes) and measured for a 5 KB URL (finding 8): the SQL is cut at 4096 bytes, the header end is not visible, the request walk is lost, the response is fine. The next request on the same connection (server side) was not measured.
A9: a decision, not measurable.
Other checks: "X-ClickHouse-Summary elapsed_ns" is the value at the first header flush: sleep(1) 1007.7 / 1009.5 ms (the headers are flushed after the query finished) vs big 7.5 / 5.7 ms while the terminal chunk arrived at +417.8 / +396.9 ms (strace). So elapsed_ns must not be used for latency (agrees with the plan). Request-to-terminal-chunk times: small +14.6 / +13.4 ms, sleep +1017.3 / +1021.7 ms, error +6.6 / +23.4 ms, wait_end +52.7 / +62.9 ms (26.9 / 26.3).

== Branch decisions
S: (S-a) holds. The server-side chunk walk with only the first 4096 bytes of each record reaches the end of every response that has an end: 33 of 41 server responses per version ("walk4096=OK"; 31 chunked with the lone 5-byte terminal chunk, 1 HEAD, 1 100-continue interim). The other 8 per version (http10, midstream x2, midstream_gzip run 2, rs_select_midstream_error runs 1-4) are not walk failures: the stream simply has no terminal chunk and no framing end (exception then close, or HTTP/1.0 close), which is the E and unanswered case. The largest header block end is at offset 688 (26.9) / 662 (26.3) of its record.
C: (C-b). The plan's condition is not met: (1) The last client read is "0 CRLF CRLF" as a lone 5-byte record in most runs, not the 7-byte form "CRLF 0 CRLF CRLF" the plan names (the 7-byte form shows up only when the last read also holds chunk data, or in compress1 on 26.9). (2) Of the 33 client connections per version, the last read is the tail and at most 4096 bytes in 22 (26.9) / 23 (26.3). In 5 (26.9: curl big 17689 bytes, gzip 19339, midstream_gzip run 1 4142 (46 bytes over the limit), rs_select 25842, wait_end 18499) / 4 (26.3: big 59689, gzip 71670, rs_select 21389, wait_end 94988) the last read ends with the tail but is bigger than 4096 bytes, with the tail at offset 4137 to 94983; the BPF record keeps only the first 4096 bytes, so the tail cannot be seen there. In 6 / 6 there is no tail at the end (HEAD, HTTP/1.0, mid-stream errors). (3) The tail would rescue only one client response whose chunk walk was lost (python http.client big: lone 5-byte record at the end); the other 5 (26.9) / 4 (26.3) lost-sync client responses (curl big, gzip, rs_select, wait_end, and on 26.9 midstream_gzip run 1) end in a record the tail is invisible in. (4) No data read that is not the last read of its response ended with the tail or equalled the 5-byte tail in any run (keepalive_ping hits are the real ends of the earlier responses). So the rule would have been safe (0 false positives in 66 connections), but it saves 1 of 6 / 1 of 5 cases, and the plan says the condition must hold for small/error/compressed results with the 7-byte form. T3: no tail inference; a client response whose walk is lost is "unanswered". The server-side event of the same query still has the end and the latency.
E: (E-a) for the server side and for client reads that keep up; (E-b) for the rest. Uncompressed mid-stream error: the "\r\n__exception__\r\n<tag>" marker is at offset 2 of a dedicated 365/366-byte record on the server in all 4 runs (26.9 and 26.3, two midstream runs each) and the tag equals the header tag. On the client the marker is at offset 2 of its own record for curl (2 of 2 runs, one per version). The slow python reader on 26.9 got it at offset 657295 of a 657661-byte read (outside 4096); on 26.3 the same slow reader still read it as its own 365-byte record at offset 2. So the client side is E-a only when the reader keeps up; a coalesced read is E-b (unanswered). The marker detection must also require the tag from the X-ClickHouse-Exception-Tag header (finding 4), because "__exception__" alone can be data.
compress=1 verdict (the clickhouse-rs shape: POST, Content-Length, compress=1, default_format=RowBinary; rs_select, rs_select_midstream_error):
  - Normal answer: status line, headers, chunks, lone 5-byte terminal chunk on the server (31/31); the completion is the terminal chunk and the server-side latency is correct. The client side cannot see it when the last read is above 4096 (rs_select: 25842 bytes on 26.9, 21389 on 26.3).
  - Error before the first flush (throwIf with compressible output, runs 0): 500 status, X-ClickHouse-Exception-Code in the headers, one body chunk (1323 bytes on 26.9, 7567 on 26.3), terminal chunk present -> normal completion plus exception from the status and header, both versions.
  - Error after output started (runs 1-4: incompressible rows): the status stays 200, there is no terminal chunk, the server closes the connection. The marker "\r\n__exception__\r\n<tag>" is visible on 26.3 (LZ4 frame, the text stays as literal bytes): server record offset 29 of a 313-, 313-, 297- and 350-byte record in 4 of 4 runs, tag equals the header tag; but the message after it is back-referenced and unreadable. On 26.9 (ZSTD frame) the marker is not visible in 0 of 4 runs. The same holds for gzip (Accept-Encoding: gzip with enable_http_compression=1): marker not visible, no terminal chunk, server closes.
  - Decision: detect with the same rule as E-a on any record (marker + tag from the header inside the first 4096 bytes); it works by accident on 26.3 + LZ4 (production: 26.3), it never works on 26.9 + ZSTD or gzip, so a mid-stream error with compression is "unanswered" unless the marker happens to be visible. On the client side the 26.3 marker was always inside a large read, at offset 74250, 52101, 43094 and 65198 (4 of 4 runs), never in the first 4096 bytes, so a compressed mid-stream error is unanswered on the client side.
A5 therefore changes from "never visible" to "visible only with LZ4 on 26.3, not guaranteed".

== Secrets and host names
Grep (decode the hex, then grep) run in internal/edc/testdata/clickhouse/http after assembling:
dec() { for f in *.records; do grep -v '^#' "$f" | cut -d' ' -f4 | tr -d '\n' | xxd -r -p; done; }   # run in the http/ directory
$ dec | grep -a -i -c -E "jinwoo|orbstack|edc-ch|lkasa|[.]local|/Users/|/home/"
0
$ grep -c -E "jinwoo|orbstack|lkasa|/Users/|/home/" *.records (comment lines, sum)
0
$ dec | grep -a -o -i -E "(password|x-clickhouse-key|quota_key|session_id|x-clickhouse-quota)[:=] ?[^& \r]*" | sort | uniq -c
 148 X-ClickHouse-Key: edc-fixture
   4 password=edc-fixture
$ dec | grep -a -o "Authorization: Basic [A-Za-z0-9+/=]*" | sort | uniq -c
   4 Authorization: Basic ZWRjOmVkYy1maXh0dXJl
$ dec | grep -a -o -i -E "x-clickhouse-server-display-name: [^\r]*|Host: [^\r]*" | sort | uniq -c
  70 Host: 127.0.0.1:8123
  70 Host: 172.18.0.2:8123
  20 Host: fixture-host:8123
 148 X-ClickHouse-Server-Display-Name: fixture-host

== Re-run procedure (Linux VM, Ubuntu 26.04 arm64)
1. 26.9: download clickhouse-common-static, clickhouse-server and clickhouse-client 26.9.16.11 arm64 .deb from https://packages.clickhouse.com/deb/pool/main/c/clickhouse/, install with a policy-rc.d that returns 101, create /etc/clickhouse-server/users.d/edc.xml (user edc, password edc-fixture, networks ::/0) and start the server in a UTS namespace as in boundaries.txt step 2 (hostname fixture-host).
2. 26.3: sudo apt-get install -y docker.io; sudo systemctl start docker (the policy-rc.d keeps the service stopped after install); sudo docker pull clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.3; sudo docker network create edc-net; sudo docker run -d --name edc-ch263 --hostname fixture-host --network edc-net -p 18123:8123 -p 19000:9000 -e CLICKHOUSE_USER=edc -e CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD=edc-fixture -e CLICKHOUSE_DEFAULT_ACCESS_MANAGEMENT=1 --ulimit nofile=262144:262144 clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.3; sudo docker run -d --name edc-client --hostname fixture-client --network edc-net --entrypoint sleep clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.3 infinity.
3. On both servers: CREATE TABLE default.t (a UInt32, b String) ENGINE=MergeTree ORDER BY a.
4. Extract the script: sed -n '/^%%BEGIN m.py/,/^%%END m.py/p' http_boundaries.txt | sed '1d;$d' > /tmp/ch/m.py (mkdir -p /tmp/ch/raw first).
5. python3 /tmp/ch/m.py data; python3 /tmp/ch/m.py run v269 all; python3 /tmp/ch/m.py run v263 all (one scenario: "run v263 small", several: comma separated). The scenario client commands are in each fixture's "# command:" lines.
6. python3 /tmp/ch/m.py analyze v269 /tmp/ch/an; the same for v263. Output: /tmp/ch/an/<ver>.analysis.txt (this table) and /tmp/ch/an/<ver>/<scenario>.records (fixtures). The x_rs_mid_rep runs are the runs 2-4 of rs_select_midstream_error (the assemble step renumbers them); x_long_url has no fixture file.
7. The 26.9 and 26.3 records of a scenario go into one file, 26.9 section first. Run the grep above.

== Verification of this procedure
The script text in this file was extracted with the sed command of step 4 (identical to the script used for the measurements) and run again on the VM: "m2.py run v263 small" then "m2.py analyze v263 <dir>".
Result for 26.3 small (GET SELECT 1, edc-client -> edc-ch263): the server side record sequence is identical to the fixture: recv 149; send 17, 22, 183, 2, 604, 3, 2, 2, 5 (10 records, same sizes). The client side differed only by read merging, as expected for client reads: fixture 149; 17, 22, 185, 604, 5, 2, 5, re-run 149; 17, 22, 183, 2, 604, 3, 2, 2, 5. Not re-run: the other 23 scenarios and 26.9.

%%BEGIN m.py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""edc trace clickhouse T1: measure ClickHouse HTTP write/read boundaries with strace.
usage: m.py data | run <ver> <scenario|all> | client <mode> <host> <port> | analyze <ver> <outdir>
"""
import bisect, glob, http.client, json, os, re, shlex, socket, subprocess, sys, time

RAW = '/tmp/ch/raw'
DATA = '/tmp/ch/data'
SYSC = 'read,recvfrom,recvmsg,readv,write,sendto,sendmsg,writev'
STR = ['-f', '-yy', '-xx', '-ttt', '-s', '2097152', '-e', 'trace=' + SYSC]
SEND = {'write', 'sendto', 'sendmsg', 'writev'}
RECV = {'read', 'recvfrom', 'recvmsg', 'readv'}
HEADCAP = 4096
AUTH = ['-H', 'X-ClickHouse-User: edc', '-H', 'X-ClickHouse-Key: edc-fixture']
PYAUTH = {'X-ClickHouse-User': 'edc', 'X-ClickHouse-Key': 'edc-fixture'}

def sh(cmd):
    return subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()

def versions():
    pid263 = int(sh("sudo docker inspect -f '{{.State.Pid}}' edc-ch263"))
    pid269 = [int(x) for x in sh("pgrep -f '^clickhouse-server --config'").split() if int(x) != pid263][0]
    ip263 = sh("sudo docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' edc-ch263")
    cpid = int(sh("sudo docker inspect -f '{{.State.Pid}}' edc-client"))
    return {
        'v269': dict(label='26.9.16.11 deb', pid=pid269, srvns=None, clins=None, host='127.0.0.1', port=8123),
        'v263': dict(label=None, pid=pid263, srvns=pid263, clins=cpid, host=ip263, port=8123),
    }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- scenarios
def Q(sql):
    return ['-G', '--data-urlencode', 'query=' + sql]

def curl(base, name, *args, out=None):
    return ['curl', '-s', '-o', out or f'/tmp/ch/out/{name}.body', '-D', f'/tmp/ch/out/{name}.hdr'] + AUTH + list(args)

def scenarios(base):
    S = {}
    def one(name, label, argv, note=''):
        S.setdefault(name, []).append((label, argv, note))
    one('small', 'curl GET', curl(base, 'small', *Q('SELECT 1'), base + '/'))
    one('sleep', 'curl GET', curl(base, 'sleep', *Q('SELECT sleep(1)'), base + '/'))
    one('big', 'curl GET', curl(base, 'big', *Q('SELECT number FROM numbers(1e7)'), base + '/', out='/dev/null'))
    one('big', 'python http.client GET', ['python3', os.path.abspath(__file__), 'client', 'big_py', base])
    one('error', 'curl GET', curl(base, 'error', *Q('SELECT * FROM missing_table'), base + '/'))
    mid = 'SELECT throwIf(number=2000000) FROM numbers(3e6)'
    one('midstream', 'curl GET', curl(base, 'midstream', *Q(mid), base + '/'))
    one('midstream', 'python raw socket slow reader (sleeps 2 s, then recv 1 MiB)', ['python3', os.path.abspath(__file__), 'client', 'slow_mid', base])
    rnd = 'SELECT toString(rand64()), throwIf(number=2000000) FROM numbers(3e6)'
    one('midstream_gzip', 'curl GET Accept-Encoding gzip + enable_http_compression=1',
        curl(base, 'midstream_gzip', '-H', 'Accept-Encoding: gzip', *Q(mid), '--data-urlencode', 'enable_http_compression=1', base + '/'))
    one('midstream_gzip', 'curl GET Accept-Encoding gzip WITHOUT enable_http_compression (server default)',
        curl(base, 'midstream_gzip_nosetting', '-H', 'Accept-Encoding: gzip', *Q(mid), base + '/'))
    one('midstream_gzip', 'curl GET gzip, incompressible rows so output is flushed before the error', curl(base, 'midstream_gzip_rnd', '-H', 'Accept-Encoding: gzip', *Q(rnd), '--data-urlencode', 'enable_http_compression=1', base + '/'))
    one('wait_end', 'curl GET wait_end_of_query=1', curl(base, 'wait_end', *Q('SELECT number FROM numbers(1e6)'), '--data-urlencode', 'wait_end_of_query=1', base + '/', out='/dev/null'))
    one('post_body', 'curl POST body', curl(base, 'post_body', '--data-binary', 'SELECT 1 FORMAT JSON', base + '/'))
    one('query_and_body', 'curl POST query=SELECT 42 + body', curl(base, 'query_and_body', '--data-binary', ' FORMAT JSONCompact', base + '/?query=SELECT%2042'))
    rows = DATA + '/rows.jsonl'
    one('insert_format', 'curl POST INSERT FORMAT JSONEachRow', curl(base, 'insert_format', '--data-binary', '@' + rows, base + '/?query=INSERT%20INTO%20t%20FORMAT%20JSONEachRow'))
    one('insert_values', 'curl POST body INSERT VALUES', curl(base, 'insert_values', '--data-binary', "INSERT INTO t VALUES (1,'a')", base + '/'))
    one('async_wait1', 'curl POST async_insert=1 wait_for_async_insert=1', curl(base, 'async_wait1', '--data-binary', '@' + rows, base + '/?async_insert=1&wait_for_async_insert=1&query=INSERT%20INTO%20t%20FORMAT%20JSONEachRow'))
    one('async_wait0', 'curl POST async_insert=1 wait_for_async_insert=0', curl(base, 'async_wait0', '--data-binary', '@' + rows, base + '/?async_insert=1&wait_for_async_insert=0&query=INSERT%20INTO%20t%20FORMAT%20JSONEachRow'))
    one('keepalive_ping', 'python http.client: SELECT 1, GET /ping, SELECT 2 on one connection', ['python3', os.path.abspath(__file__), 'client', 'keepalive', base])
    one('keepalive_ping', 'python raw socket: two requests in one send', ['python3', os.path.abspath(__file__), 'client', 'pipe_one', base])
    one('keepalive_ping', 'python raw socket: sleep(1) request then SELECT 2 request in a second send before any response', ['python3', os.path.abspath(__file__), 'client', 'pipe_two', base])
    one('gzip', 'curl GET Accept-Encoding gzip + enable_http_compression=1', curl(base, 'gzip', '-H', 'Accept-Encoding: gzip', *Q('SELECT number FROM numbers(1e6)'), '--data-urlencode', 'enable_http_compression=1', base + '/', out='/dev/null'))
    one('compress1', 'curl GET compress=1', curl(base, 'compress1', *Q('SELECT number FROM numbers(1e5)'), '--data-urlencode', 'compress=1', base + '/', out='/dev/null'))
    one('expect_continue', 'curl POST 2 MiB body, Expect: 100-continue', curl(base, 'expect_continue', '-H', 'Expect: 100-continue', '--data-binary', '@' + DATA + '/big_rows.jsonl', base + '/?query=INSERT%20INTO%20t%20FORMAT%20JSONEachRow'))
    one('http10', 'curl --http1.0 GET', curl(base, 'http10', '--http1.0', *Q('SELECT 1'), base + '/'))
    one('chunked_request', 'python http.client POST encode_chunked', ['python3', os.path.abspath(__file__), 'client', 'chunked', base])
    one('auth_headers', 'curl X-ClickHouse-User/Key headers', ['curl', '-s', '-o', '/tmp/ch/out/a1.body'] + AUTH + ['-G', '--data-urlencode', 'query=SELECT 1', base + '/'])
    one('auth_headers', 'curl Basic auth', ['curl', '-s', '-o', '/tmp/ch/out/a2.body', '-u', 'edc:edc-fixture', '-G', '--data-urlencode', 'query=SELECT 1', base + '/'])
    one('auth_headers', 'curl URL user/password', ['curl', '-s', '-o', '/tmp/ch/out/a3.body', '-G', '--data-urlencode', 'query=SELECT 1', '--data-urlencode', 'user=edc', '--data-urlencode', 'password=edc-fixture', base + '/'])
    # clickhouse-rs shapes seen in production
    one('rs_insert', 'curl POST chunked decompress=1 RowBinary LZ4 frame',
        ['curl', '-s', '-o', '/tmp/ch/out/rs_insert.body', '-D', '/tmp/ch/out/rs_insert.hdr', '-A', 'clickhouse-rs/0.15.1', '-H', 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked', '-H', 'Content-Type:', '-H', 'Accept:'] + AUTH +
        ['--data-binary', '@' + DATA + '/rs_insert.lz4', base + '/?database=default&decompress=1&query=INSERT%20INTO%20t%20FORMAT%20RowBinary'])
    rs_sel = 'SELECT number, toString(number) FROM numbers(100000)'
    one('rs_select', 'curl POST Content-Length compress=1 default_format=RowBinary',
        ['curl', '-s', '-o', '/dev/null', '-D', '/tmp/ch/out/rs_select.hdr', '-A', 'clickhouse-rs/0.15.1', '-H', 'Content-Type:', '-H', 'Accept:'] + AUTH +
        ['--data-binary', rs_sel, base + '/?compress=1&database=default&default_format=RowBinary'])
    one('rs_select_midstream_error', 'curl POST Content-Length compress=1 default_format=RowBinary, throwIf mid stream',
        ['curl', '-s', '-o', '/tmp/ch/out/rs_mid.body', '-D', '/tmp/ch/out/rs_mid.hdr', '-A', 'clickhouse-rs/0.15.1', '-H', 'Content-Type:', '-H', 'Accept:'] + AUTH +
        ['--data-binary', 'SELECT throwIf(number=2000000) FROM numbers(3e6)', base + '/?compress=1&database=default&default_format=RowBinary'])
    one('rs_select_midstream_error', 'curl POST compress=1 default_format=RowBinary, incompressible rows so output is flushed before the error',
        ['curl', '-s', '-o', '/tmp/ch/out/rs_mid2.body', '-D', '/tmp/ch/out/rs_mid2.hdr', '-A', 'clickhouse-rs/0.15.1', '-H', 'Content-Type:', '-H', 'Accept:'] + AUTH +
        ['--data-binary', rnd, base + '/?compress=1&database=default&default_format=RowBinary'])
    for k, (lim, msg) in enumerate([(1000000, ''), (1500000, ", 'boom'"), (2500000, ", 'a longer custom error message to see how it compresses'")]):
        q = f'SELECT toString(rand64()), throwIf(number={lim}{msg}) FROM numbers(3e6)'
        one('x_rs_mid_rep', f'compress=1 repeat {k}', ['curl', '-s', '-o', '/dev/null', '-A', 'clickhouse-rs/0.15.1', '-H', 'Content-Type:', '-H', 'Accept:'] + AUTH + ['--data-binary', q, base + '/?compress=1&database=default&default_format=RowBinary'])
    one('x_long_url', 'curl GET with a 5 KB URL', curl(base, 'x_long_url', *Q('SELECT 1 /*' + 'a' * 5000 + '*/'), base + '/'))
    one('head_ping', 'curl -I HEAD /ping', ['curl', '-s', '-I', '-o', '/tmp/ch/out/head_ping.hdr', base + '/ping'])
    return S

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- python clients (run under strace)
def req_bytes(method, target, extra=None, body=b''):
    h = [f'{method} {target} HTTP/1.1', 'Host: fixture-host:8123', 'User-Agent: edc-fixture', 'Accept: */*', 'Connection: keep-alive']
    h += [f'{k}: {v}' for k, v in PYAUTH.items()]
    h += extra or []
    return ('\r\n'.join(h) + '\r\n\r\n').encode() + body

def client_main(mode, base):
    host, port = base[len('http://'):].split(':')
    port = int(port)
    if mode == 'big_py':
        c = http.client.HTTPConnection(host, port)
        c.request('GET', '/?query=SELECT%20number%20FROM%20numbers(1e7)', headers=PYAUTH)
        r = c.getresponse(); n = len(r.read()); print('big_py', r.status, n)
    elif mode == 'keepalive':
        c = http.client.HTTPConnection(host, port)
        for t in ['/?query=SELECT%201', '/ping', '/?query=SELECT%202']:
            c.request('GET', t, headers=PYAUTH)
            r = c.getresponse(); print(t, r.status, r.read()[:20])
    elif mode == 'chunked':
        def body():
            for i in range(3):
                yield b'{"a":%d,"b":"x"}\n' % i
        c = http.client.HTTPConnection(host, port)
        c.request('POST', '/?query=INSERT%20INTO%20t%20FORMAT%20JSONEachRow', body=body(), headers=PYAUTH, encode_chunked=True)
        r = c.getresponse(); print('chunked', r.status, r.read()[:40])
    elif mode == 'slow_mid':
        s = socket.create_connection((host, port)); s.settimeout(10)
        s.sendall(req_bytes('GET', '/?query=SELECT%20throwIf(number%3D2000000)%20FROM%20numbers(3e6)'))
        time.sleep(2); n = 0
        while True:
            d = s.recv(1 << 20)
            if not d: break
            n += len(d)
        print('slow_mid read', n)
    elif mode in ('pipe_one', 'pipe_two'):
        s = socket.create_connection((host, port)); s.settimeout(4)
        r1 = req_bytes('GET', '/?query=SELECT%20sleep(1)%2C1' if mode == 'pipe_two' else '/?query=SELECT%201')
        r2 = req_bytes('GET', '/?query=SELECT%202')
        t0 = time.time()
        if mode == 'pipe_one':
            s.sendall(r1 + r2)
        else:
            s.sendall(r1); time.sleep(0.05); s.sendall(r2)
        data = b''; marks = []
        try:
            while True:
                d = s.recv(65536)
                if not d: marks.append(('eof', round(time.time() - t0, 3))); break
                data += d; marks.append((len(d), data.count(b'HTTP/1.1 200'), round(time.time() - t0, 3)))
        except socket.timeout:
            marks.append(('timeout', round(time.time() - t0, 3)))
        print(mode, 'responses seen', data.count(b'HTTP/1.1 '), marks)
    else:
        raise SystemExit('bad mode')

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- run
def prep_data():
    os.makedirs(DATA, exist_ok=True); os.makedirs('/tmp/ch/out', exist_ok=True)
    with open(DATA + '/rows.jsonl', 'wb') as f:
        f.write(b'\n'.join(b'{"a":%d,"b":"row%d"}' % (i, i) for i in range(3)) + b'\n')
    with open(DATA + '/big_rows.jsonl', 'wb') as f:
        line = b'{"a":1,"b":"' + b'y' * 100 + b'"}\n'
        for _ in range(2 * 1024 * 1024 // len(line) + 1):
            f.write(line)
    raw = bytearray()
    for i in range(1000):
        s = b'rs%d' % i
        raw += i.to_bytes(4, 'little') + bytes([len(s)]) + s
    open(DATA + '/rs_insert.raw', 'wb').write(raw)
    sh(f'clickhouse-compressor --codec LZ4 < {DATA}/rs_insert.raw > {DATA}/rs_insert.lz4')
    print('data ok', os.path.getsize(DATA + '/rs_insert.lz4'))

def run_one(ver, V, name, idx, label, argv):
    tag = f'{ver}.{name}.{idx}'
    srvf, clif = f'{RAW}/{tag}.srv', f'{RAW}/{tag}.cli'
    for f in (srvf, clif):
        if os.path.exists(f): subprocess.run(['sudo', 'rm', '-f', f])
    scmd = ['sudo']
    if V['srvns']: scmd += ['nsenter', '-t', str(V['srvns']), '-n']
    scmd += ['strace', '-p', str(V['pid']), '-o', srvf] + STR
    sp = subprocess.Popen(scmd, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    time.sleep(2.5)
    ccmd = []
    if V['clins']: ccmd += ['sudo', 'nsenter', '-t', str(V['clins']), '-n']
    ccmd += ['strace', '-o', clif] + STR + argv
    t0 = time.time()
    cp = subprocess.run(ccmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    el = time.time() - t0
    time.sleep(0.8)
    subprocess.run(['sudo', 'pkill', '-INT', '-f', f'strace -p {V["pid"]} -o {srvf}'])
    try: sp.wait(timeout=20)
    except Exception: sp.kill()
    subprocess.run(['sudo', 'chmod', 'a+r', srvf, clif])
    json.dump(dict(label=label, argv=argv, stdout=cp.stdout[-2000:], rc=cp.returncode, elapsed=el), open(f'{RAW}/{tag}.meta', 'w'))
    print(f'{tag} rc={cp.returncode} {el:.2f}s {cp.stdout.strip()[:150]!r}', flush=True)

def cmd_run(ver, which):
    V = versions()[ver]
    if ver == 'v263':
        V['label'] = sh("sudo docker exec edc-ch263 clickhouse-client --user edc --password edc-fixture -q 'select version()'") + ' docker ' + sh("sudo docker image inspect clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.3 --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}'").split('@')[1]
    open(f'{RAW}/{ver}.label', 'w').write(V['label'])
    base = f'http://{V["host"]}:{V["port"]}'
    S = scenarios(base)
    names = list(S) if which == 'all' else which.split(',')
    for n in names:
        for i, (label, argv, note) in enumerate(S[n]):
            run_one(ver, V, n, i, label, argv)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- strace parsing
LINE = re.compile(r'^(?:\[pid\s+(\d+)\]\s*|(\d+)\s+)?(\d+\.\d+)\s+(.*)$')
RES = re.compile(r'^<\.\.\. (\w+) resumed>(.*)$')
FD = re.compile(r'^(\w+)\((\d+)<TCP:\[(.*?)\]>')

def addr(s):
    h, p = s.rsplit(':', 1)
    return h.strip('[]'), int(p)

def parse_strace(path, side, port):
    recs = []; pend = {}; seen = set()
    with open(path, 'r', errors='replace') as f:
        for line in f:
            m = LINE.match(line.rstrip('\n'))
            if not m: continue
            pid = m.group(1) or m.group(2); ts = float(m.group(3)); rest = m.group(4)
            if rest.startswith('<... '):
                m2 = RES.match(rest)
                if not m2: continue
                p = pend.pop(pid, None)
                if p is None: continue
                full = p + m2.group(2)
            elif rest.endswith('<unfinished ...>'):
                pend[pid] = rest[:-len('<unfinished ...>')]; continue
            else:
                full = rest
            if '<TCP:[' not in full: continue
            mm = FD.match(full)
            if not mm: continue
            name, fd, sock = mm.groups()
            if name not in SEND and name not in RECV: continue
            if '->' not in sock: continue
            loc, peer = sock.split('->')
            lh, lp = addr(loc); ph, pp = addr(peer)
            if side == 'server' and lp != port: continue
            if side == 'client' and pp != port: continue
            k = full.rfind(') = ')
            if k < 0: continue
            try: ret = int(full[k + 4:].split()[0])
            except (ValueError, IndexError): continue
            if ret < 0: continue
            if ret == 0 and name in RECV:
                recs.append(dict(side=side, dir='recv', size=0, data=b'', ts=ts, conn=(pp if side == 'server' else lp), sc=name, eof=True)); continue
            if ret == 0: continue
            data = b''
            if name in ('sendmsg', 'recvmsg', 'writev', 'readv'):
                i = 0
                while True:
                    i = full.find('iov_base="', i)
                    if i < 0: break
                    j = full.find('"', i + 10)
                    data += bytes.fromhex(full[i + 10:j].replace('\\x', '')); i = j
            else:
                i = full.find('"')
                j = full.find('"', i + 1)
                try: data = bytes.fromhex(full[i + 1:j].replace('\\x', ''))
                except ValueError: raise SystemExit('unparsable: ' + full[:300])
            seen.add(name)
            recs.append(dict(side=side, dir='send' if name in SEND else 'recv', size=ret, data=data[:ret], ts=ts, conn=(pp if side == 'server' else lp), sc=name, short=len(data) < ret, peerhost=(ph if side == 'server' else lh)))
    return recs, seen

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- HTTP walkers
class Known:
    """Bytes of a stream visible when only the first HEADCAP bytes of each record are captured."""
    def __init__(self, sizes, cap):
        self.starts = []; p = 0
        for s in sizes: self.starts.append(p); p += s
        self.sizes = sizes; self.cap = cap; self.total = p
    def rec(self, pos):
        return bisect.bisect_right(self.starts, pos) - 1
    def ok(self, a, b):
        if self.cap is None: return True
        p = a
        while p < b:
            i = self.rec(p)
            if i < 0 or i >= len(self.sizes): return False
            hk = self.starts[i] + min(self.sizes[i], self.cap)
            if b <= hk: return True
            if hk < self.starts[i] + self.sizes[i]: return False
            p = hk
        return True

def read_line(buf, p, known, limit=16384):
    e = buf.find(b'\r\n', p, p + limit)
    if e < 0:
        return None, ('incomplete' if len(buf) - p < limit else 'toolong')
    if not known.ok(p, e + 2): return None, 'unknown_bytes'
    return e, None

def parse_headers(buf, p, known, ev):
    """returns (headers dict, pos after blank line, err)"""
    h = {}
    while True:
        e, err = read_line(buf, p, known)
        if err: return h, p, err
        line = buf[p:e]
        if line == b'':
            ev.append(('he', p, e + 2)); return h, e + 2, None
        ev.append(('h', p, e + 2))
        if b':' in line:
            k, v = line.split(b':', 1); h[k.strip().lower().decode('latin1')] = v.strip().decode('latin1')
        p = e + 2

def walk_chunks(buf, p, known, ev, info):
    while True:
        e = buf.find(b'\r\n', p, p + 80)
        if e < 0:
            return p, 'incomplete' if len(buf) - p < 80 else 'bad_chunk_line'
        if not known.ok(p, e + 2): return p, 'unknown_bytes'
        try: size = int(buf[p:e].split(b';')[0], 16)
        except ValueError: return p, 'bad_chunk_line'
        if size == 0:
            if buf[e + 2:e + 4] != b'\r\n': return p, 'trailers_or_incomplete'
            if not known.ok(e + 2, e + 4): return p, 'unknown_bytes'
            ev.append(('last', p, e + 4)); return e + 4, None
        ev.append(('csz', p, e + 2)); ev.append(('data', e + 2, e + 2 + size)); ev.append(('crlf', e + 2 + size, e + 4 + size))
        if e + 4 + size > len(buf): return len(buf), 'incomplete'
        p = e + 4 + size

def walk_requests(buf, known):
    ev = []; reqs = []; p = 0
    while p < len(buf):
        e, err = read_line(buf, p, known)
        if err:
            reqs.append(dict(err=err, at=p)); break
        line = buf[p:e].decode('latin1')
        r = dict(start=p, line=line, method=line.split(' ')[0]); ev.append(('rl', p, e + 2))
        h, p2, err = parse_headers(buf, e + 2, known, ev)
        r['hdr'] = h; r['he_end'] = p2
        if err: r['err'] = err; reqs.append(r); break
        te = h.get('transfer-encoding', '').lower()
        if 'chunked' in te:
            p3, err = walk_chunks(buf, p2, known, ev, r); r['kind'] = 'chunked'
        elif 'content-length' in h:
            n = int(h['content-length']); ev.append(('body', p2, p2 + n)); p3, err = p2 + n, None; r['kind'] = 'cl'
            if p2 + n > len(buf): err = 'incomplete'
        else:
            p3, err = p2, None; r['kind'] = 'none'
        r['end'] = p3
        if err: r['err'] = err
        reqs.append(r)
        if err: break
        p = p3
    return ev, reqs

def walk_responses(buf, known, methods):
    ev = []; resps = []; p = 0; n = 0
    while p < len(buf):
        e, err = read_line(buf, p, known)
        if err:
            resps.append(dict(err=err, at=p, start=p)); break
        line = buf[p:e].decode('latin1')
        try: code = int(line.split(' ')[1])
        except Exception:
            resps.append(dict(err='bad_status_line', at=p, start=p, line=line[:40])); break
        r = dict(start=p, line=line, code=code); ev.append(('st', p, e + 2))
        h, p2, err = parse_headers(buf, e + 2, known, ev)
        r['hdr'] = h; r['he_end'] = p2
        if err: r['err'] = err; resps.append(r); break
        if 100 <= code < 200:
            r['kind'] = 'interim'; r['end'] = p2; resps.append(r); p = p2; continue
        method = methods[n] if n < len(methods) else 'GET'; n += 1
        te = h.get('transfer-encoding', '').lower()
        if method == 'HEAD' or code in (204, 304):
            r['kind'] = 'nobody'; p3, err = p2, None
        elif 'chunked' in te:
            r['kind'] = 'chunked'; p3, err = walk_chunks(buf, p2, known, ev, r)
        elif 'content-length' in h:
            cl = int(h['content-length']); r['kind'] = 'cl'; ev.append(('body', p2, p2 + cl)); p3 = p2 + cl; err = 'incomplete' if p2 + cl > len(buf) else None
        else:
            r['kind'] = 'until_close'; p3, err = len(buf), 'no_framing'
        r['end'] = p3
        if err: r['err'] = err
        resps.append(r)
        if err: break
        p = p3
    return ev, resps

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- analysis
def concat(recs):
    return b''.join(r['data'] for r in recs)

def compress_kinds(kinds, mid):
    t = []
    for k in kinds:
        if t and t[-1][0] == k: t[-1][1] += 1
        else: t.append([k, 1])
    s = '+'.join(k if n == 1 else f'{k}x{n}' for k, n in t)
    return ('~' + s) if mid else s

def pattern(sizes, ev, maxlen=150):
    starts = []; p = 0
    for s in sizes: starts.append(p); p += s
    startset = {}
    for kind, a, b in ev:
        startset.setdefault(a, []).append(kind)
    toks = []
    for i, st in enumerate(starts):
        kinds = [k for k, a, b in ev if st <= a < st + sizes[i]] if len(ev) < 5000 else None
        if kinds is None:
            kinds = []
            lo = bisect.bisect_left([a for _, a, _ in ev], st); hi = bisect.bisect_left([a for _, a, _ in ev], st + sizes[i])
            kinds = [ev[x][0] for x in range(lo, hi)]
        mid = st not in startset
        toks.append(compress_kinds(kinds, mid) or ('~mid' if mid else 'none'))
    rl = []
    for t in toks:
        if rl and rl[-1][0] == t: rl[-1][1] += 1
        else: rl.append([t, 1])
    s = ' | '.join(t if n == 1 else f'{t} x{n}' for t, n in rl)
    return s if len(s) <= maxlen else s[:maxlen] + f' ...(+{len(s)-maxlen} chars, {len(rl)} runs)'

def rec_of(starts, sizes, pos):
    i = bisect.bisect_right(starts, pos) - 1
    return i, pos - starts[i]

def analyze_conn(ver, key, recs, label):
    """recs: all records of one connection, both sides. returns (text, fixture_lines)"""
    L = []
    side = lambda s, d: [r for r in recs if r['side'] == s and r['dir'] == d and r['size'] > 0]
    cs, sr, ss, cr = side('client', 'send'), side('server', 'recv'), side('server', 'send'), side('client', 'recv')
    req_c, req_s, rsp_s, rsp_c = concat(cs), concat(sr), concat(ss), concat(cr)
    L.append(f'  bytes: request {len(req_s)} (client==server: {req_c == req_s}); response {len(rsp_s)} (server==client: {rsp_s == rsp_c})')
    short = [r for r in recs if r.get('short')]
    if short: L.append(f'  WARNING: {len(short)} records with short data')
    eofs = [(r['side'], round(r['ts'], 3)) for r in recs if r.get('eof')]
    out = {}
    # reference parse on the server-side request stream (full)
    full = Known([1], None)
    ev, reqs = walk_requests(req_s or req_c, full)
    methods = [r['method'] for r in reqs if 'method' in r]
    for r in reqs:
        L.append(f'  request: {r.get("line","?")[:72]!r} kind={r.get("kind")} hdr_end={r.get("he_end")} end={r.get("end")} err={r.get("err")}')
    # request side per-record
    for who, rr, buf in (('client send', cs, req_c), ('server recv', sr, req_s)):
        sizes = [r['size'] for r in rr]
        kn = Known(sizes, HEADCAP)
        ev, rq = walk_requests(buf, kn)
        starts = kn.starts
        he = [(i, a) for i, (k, a, b) in enumerate(ev) if k == 'he']
        multi = 0
        for i, s in enumerate(starts):
            n = sum(1 for k, a, b in ev if k == 'rl' and s <= a < s + sizes[i])
            if n > 1: multi += 1
        he_s = ','.join(f'rec{rec_of(starts, sizes, ev[i][2]-1)[0]}@{rec_of(starts, sizes, ev[i][2]-1)[1]+1}' for i, _ in he)
        L.append(f'  {who}: records={len(sizes)} sizes={sizes[:10]}{"..." if len(sizes) > 10 else ""} pattern=[{pattern(sizes, ev, 120)}] header_end(rec@end offset)={he_s} walk4096_ok={all("err" not in r for r in rq) and len(rq) > 0} records_with_2plus_requests={multi}')
    # responses
    res = []
    for who, rr, buf in (('server send', ss, rsp_s), ('client recv', cr, rsp_c)):
        sizes = [r['size'] for r in rr]
        kn = Known(sizes, HEADCAP); starts = kn.starts
        evf, rspf = walk_responses(buf, Known([max(1, len(buf))], None), methods)
        ev4, rsp4 = walk_responses(buf, kn, methods)
        sd = f'  {who}: records={len(sizes)} sizes={sizes[:12]}{"..." if len(sizes) > 12 else ""}\n    pattern=[{pattern(sizes, evf)}]'
        L.append(sd)
        # positions from full parse
        for n, r in enumerate(rspf):
            if r.get('kind') == 'interim' or 'start' in r and 'he_end' not in r:
                pass
            if 'he_end' in r:
                i, o = rec_of(starts, sizes, r['he_end'] - 1) if sizes else (0, 0)
                hdrend = f'header end rec{i}@{o+1}/{sizes[i]} in4096={o+1 <= HEADCAP}'
            else: hdrend = 'header end n/a'
            lasts = [(a, b) for k, a, b in evf if k == 'last' and r['start'] <= a < (r.get('end') or 1 << 60)]
            if lasts:
                a, b = lasts[0]; i, o = rec_of(starts, sizes, a); i2, o2 = rec_of(starts, sizes, b - 1)
                lastd = f'last chunk rec{i}@{o}-rec{i2}@{o2+1}/{sizes[i2]} in4096={o2+1 <= HEADCAP} alone5={sizes[i] == 5 and o == 0}'
            elif r.get('kind') == 'cl':
                i, o = rec_of(starts, sizes, r['end'] - 1); lastd = f'body end rec{i}@{o+1}/{sizes[i]} in4096={o+1 <= HEADCAP}'
            elif r.get('kind') in ('nobody', 'interim'): lastd = r['kind']
            else: lastd = f'no end seen ({r.get("err")})'
            r4 = rsp4[n] if n < len(rsp4) else {}
            w4 = 'OK' if (r4.get('end') == r.get('end') and 'err' not in r4) else f'LOST({r4.get("err")})'
            L.append(f'    response{n}: {r["line"][9:40]!r} {r.get("kind")}; {hdrend}; {lastd}; walk4096={w4}')
            if r.get('hdr') and who == 'server send':
                tag = r['hdr'].get('x-clickhouse-exception-tag'); summ = r['hdr'].get('x-clickhouse-summary', '')
                m = re.search(r'"elapsed_ns":"(\d+)"', summ)
                if m: L.append(f'      X-ClickHouse-Summary elapsed_ns={int(m.group(1))/1e6:.1f} ms; exception-tag={tag}; exception-code={r["hdr"].get("x-clickhouse-exception-code")}; content-encoding={r["hdr"].get("content-encoding")}')
        # exception marker
        for m in re.finditer(rb'__exception__', rsp_s):
            pass
        marks = [m.start() for m in re.finditer(rb'__exception__\r\n', buf)]
        tagm = re.search(rb'x-clickhouse-exception-tag: ([a-z]{16})', buf[:8192], re.I)
        if marks:
            infos = []
            for pos in marks[:4]:
                i, o = rec_of(starts, sizes, pos)
                infos.append(f'rec{i}@{o}/{sizes[i]} in4096={o + 15 + 16 <= HEADCAP} tag_matches_header={bool(tagm) and buf[pos+15:pos+31] == tagm.group(1)}')
            L.append(f'    __exception__ marker+CRLF: {len(marks)} -> ' + '; '.join(infos))
        else:
            L.append('    __exception__ marker: none in the stream')
        # tail check (client side C-a)
        if who == 'client recv':
            tail = b'\r\n0\r\n\r\n'
            ends = [i for i, r in enumerate(rr) if r['data'].endswith(tail)]
            ends5 = [i for i, r in enumerate(rr) if r['data'] == b'0\r\n\r\n']
            lastn = len(rr) - 1
            L.append(f'    tail: reads ending 7B CRLF-0-CRLF-CRLF: {ends}; reads equal to 5B 0-CRLF-CRLF: {ends5}; last read index {lastn} size {sizes[-1] if sizes else None}')
        res.append((who, rr, buf, rspf, evf, starts, sizes))
    # timing
    if cs:
        t0 = cs[0]['ts']
        def done_ts(rr, evf, starts, sizes, rspf, usend):
            for r in rspf:
                if r.get('kind') in ('chunked', 'cl', 'nobody') and 'err' not in r and r.get('end'):
                    i, o = rec_of(starts, sizes, r['end'] - 1)
                    return rr[i]['ts'], i
            return None, None
        tl = []
        for who, rr, buf, rspf, evf, starts, sizes in res:
            td, i = done_ts(rr, evf, starts, sizes, rspf, who)
            if td is None:
                mk = buf.find(b'\r\n__exception__\r\n')
                if mk >= 0:
                    i, o = rec_of(starts, sizes, mk); td = rr[i]['ts']
            fr = rr[0]['ts'] - t0 if rr else None
            tl.append(f'{who}: first response record +{fr*1000:.1f} ms, completion record +{(td - t0)*1000:.1f} ms' if td else f'{who}: no completion seen')
        L.append('  timing (strace start-of-call stamps, relative to first client send): ' + '; '.join(tl))
    if eofs: L.append(f'  eof seen: {eofs}')
    return '\n'.join(L), None

def fixture_lines(recs, comp):
    """lines in time order; client/server merged. comp: set of (side,dir,index) to compact."""
    allr = sorted(recs, key=lambda r: r['ts'])
    out = []
    for r in allr:
        if r['size'] == 0: continue
        hexs = r['data'][:HEADCAP].hex()
        if r.get('compact'): hexs = r['data'][:64].hex()
        out.append(f"{r['side']} {r['dir']} {r['size']} {hexs}")
    return out

def mark_compact(recs):
    """records > 4096 bytes keep only 64 bytes when no framing element or error marker starts between byte 56 and byte 4096."""
    for side, d, walker in (('server', 'send', 'resp'), ('client', 'recv', 'resp'), ('client', 'send', 'req'), ('server', 'recv', 'req')):
        rr = [r for r in recs if r['side'] == side and r['dir'] == d and r['size'] > 0]
        buf = concat(rr)
        kn = Known([max(1, len(buf))], None)
        ev = walk_responses(buf, kn, [])[0] if walker == 'resp' else walk_requests(buf, kn)[0]
        starts = []; p = 0
        for r in rr: starts.append(p); p += r['size']
        a_list = [a for _, a, _ in ev]
        for i, r in enumerate(rr):
            if r['size'] <= HEADCAP: continue
            lo = bisect.bisect_left(a_list, starts[i]); hi = bisect.bisect_left(a_list, starts[i] + r['size'])
            late = [ev[x] for x in range(lo, hi) if ev[x][0] not in ('data', 'body') and 56 <= ev[x][1] - starts[i] < HEADCAP]
            if not late and b'__exception__' not in r['data'][56:HEADCAP]:
                r['compact'] = True

def cmd_analyze(ver, outdir):
    label = open(f'{RAW}/{ver}.label').read()
    port = 8123
    tags = sorted({os.path.basename(p)[:-4] for p in glob.glob(f'{RAW}/{ver}.*.*.srv')})
    ana = open(f'{outdir}/{ver}.analysis.txt', 'w')
    byscn = {}
    for tag in tags:
        _, name, idx = tag.split('.', 2)[0], tag.split('.')[1], tag.split('.')[2]
        meta = json.load(open(f'{RAW}/{tag}.meta'))
        srv, s1 = parse_strace(f'{RAW}/{tag}.srv', 'server', port)
        cli, s2 = parse_strace(f'{RAW}/{tag}.cli', 'client', port)
        conns = {}
        for r in srv:
            conns.setdefault(r['conn'], []).append(r)
        for r in cli:
            conns.setdefault(r['conn'], []).append(r)
        keys = sorted(conns, key=lambda k: min(r['ts'] for r in conns[k]))
        ana.write(f'== {name} / run {idx}: {meta["label"]} [{ver}] syscalls seen: server={sorted(s1)} client={sorted(s2)}; client rc={meta["rc"]}; connections={len(keys)}\n')
        if meta['stdout'].strip(): ana.write('  client stdout: ' + repr(meta['stdout'][:260]) + '\n')
        for ck in keys:
            recs = conns[ck]
            # keep only connections that carried data both ways
            txt, _ = analyze_conn(ver, ck, recs, meta['label'])
            ana.write(f' -- connection client_port={ck} (records={len(recs)})\n' + txt + '\n')
            mark_compact(recs)
            byscn.setdefault(name, []).append((int(idx), meta, ck, recs))
        ana.flush()
    # fixtures
    os.makedirs(f'{outdir}/{ver}', exist_ok=True)
    for name, runs in byscn.items():
        lines = []
        lines.append(f'# version: {label}')
        for idx, meta, ck, recs in sorted(runs, key=lambda x: (x[0], x[2])):
            pass
        last_idx = None
        for idx, meta, ck, recs in sorted(runs, key=lambda x: (x[0], min(r['ts'] for r in x[3]))):
            if idx != last_idx:
                cmd = shlex.join(meta['argv'])
                lines.append(f'# run {idx}: {meta["label"]}')
                lines.append('# command: ' + cmd.replace(os.path.abspath(__file__), 'm.py').replace('/tmp/ch/data/', 'DATA/'))
                last_idx = idx
            else:
                lines.append(f'# (second connection of run {idx})')
            lines += fixture_lines(recs, None)
        open(f'{outdir}/{ver}/{name}.records', 'w').write('\n'.join(lines) + '\n')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    c = sys.argv[1]
    if c == 'data': prep_data()
    elif c == 'run': cmd_run(sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3])
    elif c == 'client': client_main(sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3])
    elif c == 'analyze': cmd_analyze(sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3])
%%END m.py

tcp_recvmsg_exit   1016 -> 1021                  638 -> 666                        184386 -> 174712
http_tcp_destroy_sock  154 -> 133                154 -> 135                        145 -> 145
trace clickhouse with clickhouse_http_port=0 (not a command, for the branch pruning check): 262, 196590, 225, 654, 133 in the program order above.
Largest program: tcp_sendmsg_exit at 196634, 20% of the limit, unchanged. All three commands load.
Why the counts moved: the source change is only in mysql_socket, which tcp_sendmsg_entry, tcp_recvmsg_entry, tcp_recvmsg_exit and http_tcp_destroy_sock inline. The instruction count of every program changed only for those four (+5, +10, +13, +10 instructions in the object, tcp_recvmsg_exit_legacy as tcp_recvmsg_exit); all other programs keep their length. The trace http numbers moved without a code path that trace http runs (mysql_port is 0 there), so the cause is the compiler layout of the inlined function, not the new comparison. This is inferred, not confirmed by a build of the old source with the same clang.
Object diff: the generated .go files differ from the previous ones only by the ClickhouseHttpPort variable (captureEventsVarClickhouseHttpPort, ClickhouseHttpPort in the VariableSpecs and Variables structs). The .o files cannot be compared byte by byte because the new .rodata variable shifts offsets. No other bpf2go object changed.
Regression, same curl requests (3 POST SELECT, 127.0.0.1:8123, ClickHouse 26.9) with the binary before and after:
 - trace http --port 8123 --payload --raw --duration 8s: both give 12 events (6 http_request + 6 http_2xx, order client request, server request, server 2xx, client 2xx, three times), the same field names, and capture_summary lost_events=0. The client http_2xx "bytes" and "payload" differ between runs (17, 221, 841 bytes) because curl reads the response in different pieces; this also differs between two runs of the same old binary.
 - trace mysql --duration 3s: loads, the output (header lines) is the same.
 - trace clickhouse --duration 9s with clickhouse-client SELECT 1, SELECT sleep(0.2), SELECT * FROM missing_table on 9000 and two curl queries on 8123: both give 61 lines, 6 connect, 6 hello, 6 query, 4 end, 2 exception; only latencies differ. The two HTTP queries make no event yet (the records on 8123 are dropped until the HTTP tracker exists).
